extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / policymakers interested in postwar public policy
extracted.subtask_description: Short-form wire/press reporting covering multiple postwar public-policy topics (labor disputes, antitrust probes, housing/priorities, surplus-property disposition, rationing and investigations). Meant for a general audience and policymakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bipartisan leadership in national policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Government in a democracy should not decree such a policy. But it should take a leadership ... of these should be maintained ... bi-partisan, united recourse ... support of the people of all walks of life to make them effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy formation ought to be led in a bipartisan, united manner to secure broad public support and effectiveness. Avoid partisan exclusivity; include minority and majority parties in responsibility for major decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of temporary government price controls when scarcity requires
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary that there be temporary government price control in place of competitive price control. To fail to exercise that leadership and foresight means that the policy is formed in a violent clash between economic forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend temporary price controls during acute supply shortages to prevent harmful inflation; act with leadership and foresight to avoid disruptive economic clashes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid passing major legislation in the heat of controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation of this kind should not be passed in the heat of a controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pause contentious legislative proposals until after immediate crises have cooled to allow better deliberation and avoid unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-finding commissions as dispute-resolution machinery
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-finding commissions in individual disputes with time in which to operate is good machinery. We have had this machinery complete with waiting periods, subpoena powers, and the duty to make specific recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use commissions endowed with waiting periods, subpoena powers and an obligation to issue concrete recommendations; give them sufficient time to investigate. Note: the page also cautions that such machinery 'is not the answer to the present problem'—i.e., it may be insufficient for some crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antitrust investigation trigger and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Justice has been investigating several anti-trust cases of the type you mention, among which is General Motors. Glad to receive any additional information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evidence suggests monopoly/anticompetitive practices (e.g., control of parts manufacturing disadvantaging competitors), DOJ may open investigations and request additional information from complainants; corporations may decline public comment while investigations proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage negotiation standard: discuss 'ability to pay' and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: In bargaining the corporation refused to discuss wages on 'ability to pay' even should the union abandon its demand that GM open its books in the discussion or if car prices were kept out of the parleys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective wage negotiations should consider the employer's ability to pay and transparency (e.g., opening books) as legitimate topics. Refusal to discuss ability-to-pay can be a primary stumbling block to settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of building-material priorities favoring housing
rubrics_metrics.description: The plan is not to prohibit commercial and industrial construction, but to allow it only in cases where materials are available after home needs have been met. There is a possibility that any priorities set up may earmark materials for low- and moderately priced houses only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In postwar material shortages, prioritize building materials for home construction (especially low/moderate-cost housing and veterans) before commercial/industrial projects; consider price/sale ceilings to target assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surplus property disposition criterion (federal plants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Surplus Property Administration recommended that seven of thirteen government-owned magnesium plants be taken out of production. It said privately owned plants can produce sufficient magnesium to meet estimated consumption in the next few years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When private sector capacity suffices for peacetime needs, consider selling, dismantling, converting, or placing federally owned production plants on standby to reduce government investment and operating costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair Employment Practice Committee limits under law
rubrics_metrics.description: The law requires that when the Government seizes a property under wartime powers the conditions under which the property was to be operated were the same as those of any other property so seized... the committee cannot contravene an act of Congress in order to carry out the present committee's aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative committees (e.g., FEPC) must operate within the constraints of existing statutes; they may not issue orders that would conflict with acts of Congress or exceed statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: House Expenditures Committee standard on employment guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee said it 'unqualifiedly rejects' any theory under which employment through private enterprise would be perfunctory and the guaranty would really rest on Federal investment and expenditure. Adoption of such a theory would entail continued deficit spending and destroy the United States system of free competitive enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy proposals guaranteeing employment through heavy federal investment are viewed as risking unbalanced budgets and a move toward 'stateism'; committees stress preserving private enterprise and caution against permanent federal guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationing programs require advance statistical planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The first thing you must understand about rationing... Statistics had to be run down, trapped and analyzed. Production figures were interpreted. Possible effects of the plan were debated. That is why OPA did so much advance work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not design rationing ad hoc; base ration schemes on solid statistical analysis, production forecasts, and impact assessments. Advance work and scenario planning are essential to effective rationing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations into alleged misuse/destruction of surplus war property
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for investigation so that those at fault may be punished. Representative Latham said information reached him that supplies had been 'dumped in the sea or burned' and urged subpoenas and inquiry into reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of wanton destruction or mismanagement of government surplus warrant formal investigation (subpoenas, hearings) to verify claims and assign accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of cultural property in wartime custody
rubrics_metrics.description: A shipment of paintings... will be stored in the National Gallery of Art... The Army said that 'it is not contemplated that any of these works of art will be exhibited to the public at present.' The pictures will be returned to the museums when conditions in Europe warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When transporting/safeguarding cultural treasures, arrange secure storage and preservation, avoid public exhibition while in protective custody, and plan for eventual return to original owners when conditions permit.
